quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (consolidated, K-IFRS): Q2 2026 revenue KRW 179,010,795,049 vs KRW 164,227,404,225 in Q2 2025; Q2 operating profit KRW 27,254,732,720 vs KRW 23,502,016,591. H1 2026 revenue KRW 349,879,852,207 vs KRW 322,017,907,097; H1 operating profit KRW 52,172,911,677 vs KRW 44,962,083,971; H1 net income KRW 35,127,649,624 vs KRW 28,849,473,050. Own-product sales rose to KRW 313,465,057,086 in H1 from KRW 253,461,964,263 while merchandise sales fell to KRW 31,580,075,045 from KRW 63,445,654,442. H1 sales were KRW 283,146,669K domestic and KRW 66,733,183K direct export. Three customers above 10% of revenue (names undisclosed): customer AAA KRW 83,167,912K (23.77%), BBB KRW 61,981,511K (17.72%), CCC KRW 37,607,862K (10.75%) (H1 2025: AAA 23.49%, BBB 16.45%). Revenue by region before eliminations: Korea KRW 322,451,354K, East Asia KRW 68,867,836K, North/Central America KRW 17,786,612K. Average selling price of process chemicals KRW 2,479/kg (FY2025: KRW 2,447/kg) and of fine chemicals (photoresist raw materials) KRW 648,569/kg (KRW 516,910/kg). The US unit (ENF USA Holdings, Kyle, Texas plant) had H1 revenue KRW 9,879,570K and a net loss of KRW 8,837,922K. R&D spend KRW 12,474,080K = 3.57% of revenue. FY2025 reference: electronic-materials revenue KRW 670,896,290K, up 15.2%.

Capacity and inputs: H1 2026 utilisation was 47.07% for process chemicals (Ulsan, Asan, Cheonan) and 72.00% for fine chemicals (Ulsan); the company says it deliberately keeps spare process-chemical capacity because new products must be qualified on customers' mass-production lines using product from mass-production equipment. Main solvent (thinner etc.) purchases were KRW 34,268 million (17.3% of parent purchases), with Purit among the suppliers, at KRW 2,672/kg vs KRW 2,335/kg in FY2025; raw-material purchases from affiliate Purit were KRW 38,780,021K in H1. Property, plant and equipment rose to KRW 437,372,234K, with H1 additions of KRW 22,834,957K and construction in progress of KRW 57,874,901K; the company has signed an investment MOU with Yesan county and invested about KRW 318 hundred-million to secure an industrial complex site. Sales follow customers' production plans via purchase orders, not long-term volume contracts.

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio changes: PAM Technology (a Korean semiconductor electronic-materials maker in Asan) became a 78.87% subsidiary in H1 2026 after ENF bought an additional 32.44% from Morita Chemical Industrial on top of its 46.43% stake; PAM had H1 revenue of KRW 39,226,277K. ENF's stake in CMP-slurry maker UB Materials rose to 79.39% from 60.75%. R&D completed in 2026: a Cu cleaner for the hybrid-bonding process (removes Si and organic particles after dicing to raise hybrid-bonding yield) and a Cu etchant for new Cu/Ti films; completed in 2025: organic EUV polymer, EUV photoresist developer, Cu VMS for TSV Cu bumps, PSPI polymer and a high-selectivity DRAM etchant. The company expects demand for high-value materials to rise over the mid to long term as AI spreads and HBM and AI-server memory grow.
